# Overnote notes with overnote-axi

overnote-axi reads, searches, creates, updates, organizes, and links notes in Overnote, the floating notepad for Raycast.
Output is compact TOON on stdout; reads work while Overnote is closed, and writes go through the running app.
If `command -v overnote-axi` fails, run `npm install -g .` in the overnote-axi repository, or run `node <overnote-axi repo>/dist/overnote-axi.js` wherever this skill says `overnote-axi`.

## Start here

Run `overnote-axi` first: it shows the helper state, note counts, the current note, pinned and recent notes, and its next steps:

- `overnote-axi read <id>`
- `overnote-axi search "<text>"`
- `overnote-axi create --content "<markdown>"`

Then:

- Add to a note with `overnote-axi update <id> --content "<markdown>"`; `--prepend` inserts right after the title line, so the title stays, and `--top` puts the content above the title, which renames the note.
- Check a task or fix a line with `overnote-axi edit <id> --old "<exact markdown>" --new "<markdown>"`; a retry of a whole line edit that already landed is a no-op.
- Pass the `updatedAt` that `read` printed as `--expected-updated-at`, so a concurrent edit fails with `STALE_WRITE` instead of being overwritten.
- Link notes with `overnote-axi link <id> --into <other id>`.

## Commands

```text
home       Dashboard: helper state, counts, pinned and recent notes (the default)
list       List live notes, pinned first, or only pinned ones
search     Find notes whose title or text contains a query
read       Show one or more notes as markdown
links      Show the notes a note links to and the notes linking back
status     Helper, database and path diagnostics
create     Create a note from markdown
update     Append (default), prepend below the title, add on top, or replace a note's markdown
edit       Replace exact text inside a note
link       Print a note's markdown link, or insert it into another note
pin        Pin a note to the end of the pinned list
unpin      Unpin a note
move       Move a pinned note up or down the pinned list
duplicate  Copy a note into a new note
delete     Move a note to Recently Deleted (--permanent erases it)
recover    Restore a note from Recently Deleted
trash      List Recently Deleted, or empty it with --empty --permanent
open       Show a note (or the last one) in the Overnote panel
setup      Install or remove the session hook (default) or the agent skill
```

`<note>` is current (the note open in Overnote, else the newest note), a full id, `title:<exact title>`, or a unique id fragment of 6+ chars; prefer the last 6 chars of the id, since notes made close together share a prefix.
Every command takes `--help`, and flags go after the command.
Exit codes: 0 success including no-ops, 1 error, 2 usage error; every error prints `code` and `help` lines.

## Examples

```sh
# Start here: helper state, counts, current, pinned and recent notes
overnote-axi
# Find notes by title or text (title matches first)
overnote-axi search "standup"
# Read the note open in Overnote (else the newest note), then the whole of a long one by id suffix
overnote-axi read current
overnote-axi read K9QW7Z --full
# Create a note: the title becomes its first line
overnote-axi create --title "Trip ideas" --content "As of Oct 20."
# Append a line (append is the default mode and keeps every existing block)
overnote-axi update K9QW7Z --content "- [ ] call Sam"
# Append a dated section written to a file first, such as ## Oct 20: Follow ups
overnote-axi update K9QW7Z --content-file /tmp/section.md
# Refresh the As of line under the title
overnote-axi edit K9QW7Z --old "As of Oct 20." --new "As of Oct 21."
# Check off a task, guarded by the updatedAt that read printed
overnote-axi edit K9QW7Z --old "- [ ] call Sam" --new "- [x] call Sam" --expected-updated-at 1792543271491
# Link one note into another
overnote-axi link M1CX4P --into K9QW7Z
# Organize
overnote-axi pin K9QW7Z
# Move to Recently Deleted, and bring it back
overnote-axi delete K9QW7Z
overnote-axi recover K9QW7Z
```

Content goes in `--content <markdown>`, `--content -` (stdin), or `--content-file <path>`; use a file for anything longer than a line or two.

## Supported markdown

- Headings `#`, `##` and `###`; deeper headings are stored as level 3.
- Paragraphs; a single newline inside a paragraph is a line break.
- Inline `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `~~strike~~`, `++underline++`, `` `code` `` and `[label](https://example.com)` links; bare `https://` URLs become links.
- Bullet lists `- item`, numbered lists `1. item`, and task lists `- [ ] open` and `- [x] done`; nest an item by indenting it to its parent's text (2 spaces under `-`, 3 under `1.`).
- Block quotes `> text`, fenced code blocks with a language, and a horizontal rule `---` on its own line.
- Not rendered: tables stay literal `|` text, images keep only their alt text, and HTML other than inline tags such as `<b>` or `<br>` is dropped (its text stays).
- Toggle lists exist only in the editor and read back as bullets; an edit touching a collapsed one fails with `LOSSY_REWRITE`.

## Writing clean notes

In a note the person wrote, follow its existing layout; these rules are for notes you create and maintain.
They match [Overnote's guide](https://github.com/WesleyBLDC/overnote#writing-clean-notes).

- The first line is the title: start a new note with `create --title "<short, specific title>"`, which stores `# Title`.
- For a living note, put `As of <Mon DD>.` on the second line and refresh it with `edit` (`update --prepend` also lands below the title).
- Group with `##` sections and at most one `###` level below them; never skip levels.
- One blank line between blocks (extra ones are stored as empty lines); no trailing spaces.
- One short idea per bullet; put detail in a nested bullet.
- Numbered lists only for steps or order, bullets otherwise, `- [ ]` tasks for things to do.
- Bold only the few words a reader must see, never whole lines or headings.
- `inline code` for commands, paths, ids, and keys; a fenced block with a language for anything multi line.
- Links as `[short label](url)`; reference another note with `overnote-axi link` (its deeplink) instead of copying its text.
- No tables or images: use a short list of `label: value` bullets.
- Add updates as a dated section at the end (`## Oct 21: <what changed>`) or fix a line with `edit`; never rewrite a note to add one fact.

## Safety rules

- Append by default: `update` appends unless told otherwise, and keeps every existing block exactly as stored.
- `edit` is block scoped: only the blocks containing `--old` are rewritten, so prefer it for checking a task or fixing a line.
- Use `update --replace` or `delete` only when the user asks for a rewrite or a deletion of that note; `--replace` also needs the `--expected-updated-at` that `read` printed.
- `LOSSY_REWRITE` means markdown cannot hold part of the note; prefer `update` (append) or a narrower `edit` over `--allow-loss`.
- `delete` moves a note to Recently Deleted for 60 days and `recover <id>` restores it, so say so when you delete.
- Pass `--permanent` (`delete --permanent <full id>`, `trash --empty --permanent --expected-count <n>`) only when the user explicitly asked in this conversation to erase notes for good; never infer it from "delete" or "clean up", and no hint ever offers it.
- A write to the note open in Overnote prints a warning: Overnote merges it with unsaved typing, and an older Overnote that saves over it is reported as `OVERWRITTEN_BY_EDITOR`.
- Never read or write Overnote's database or files directly, and never drive the Raycast window; this CLI is the only interface.

## Common errors

- `STALE_WRITE`: the note changed since you read it; read it again, then retry with the new `updatedAt`.
- `LOSSY_REWRITE`: the rewrite would drop content markdown cannot hold; append instead, or narrow `--old`.
- `HELPER_NOT_RUNNING`: Overnote is closed or its socket was refused; follow the hint (`overnote-axi open` to start it, or `overnote-axi status` to see why it was refused), then retry the write.
- `AMBIGUOUS_NOTE` and `AMBIGUOUS_TEXT`: pick a full id from the candidates, or add context to `--old`.
- `NOTE_TRASHED`: the note is in Recently Deleted; recover it only if the user wants it back.
- `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` and `HELPER_TIMEOUT`: the write may have landed (a `HELPER_TIMEOUT` on `create` or `duplicate` included); run `overnote-axi read <id>` (or `overnote-axi list --sort created` after `create` or `duplicate`) before any retry.
